questions.prompt: What is 2,026 − 26?
questions.hint: Look at the last two digits.

questions.prompt: How many inches are in 2 yards? (1 yard = 3 feet and 1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.hint: Change yards to feet first, then feet to inches.

questions.prompt:
What number comes next in this pattern?
2, 5, 8, 11, ___
questions.hint: How much is added each time?

questions.prompt: A coin is flipped 3 times in a row. How many different results are possible? (One result is heads, tails, heads.)
questions.hint: Each flip has 2 results. Multiply.
questions.solution: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 results: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT.

questions.prompt: What is 6 + 4 × 5?
questions.hint: Multiply before you add.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 48 square inches and a perimeter of 28 inches. How long is its longer side?
questions.hint: The length and width add up to half the perimeter. Which two numbers add to 14 and multiply to 48?
questions.solution: Length + width = 28 ÷ 2 = 14. Two numbers that add to 14 and multiply to 48 are 8 and 6. The longer side is 8 inches.

questions.prompt: There are 140 kids at the school play. There are 20 more boys than girls. How many girls are at the play?
questions.hint: Take away the 20 extra boys first.
questions.solution: 140 − 20 = 120. Half of 120 is 60, so there are 60 girls (and 80 boys).

questions.prompt: Eight teams play in a fall soccer tournament. The losing team of each game is out, and there are no ties. How many games are played in all to find the champion?
questions.hint: Every game knocks out exactly one team. How many teams must be knocked out?
questions.solution: All teams except the champion must lose once, so 8 − 1 = 7 teams are knocked out. That takes 7 games (4 + 2 + 1).

questions.prompt: What is 6 × 98?
questions.hint: 98 is 2 less than 100.
questions.solution: 6 × 100 = 600. Six groups of 2 too many is 12, so 600 − 12 = 588.

questions.prompt: Dad started driving at 10:40 PM and arrived at 1:15 AM the next morning. How many minutes did he drive?
questions.hint: Count to midnight first.
questions.solution: 10:40 PM to 12:00 midnight is 1 hour 20 minutes = 80 minutes. Midnight to 1:15 AM is 75 minutes. 80 + 75 = 155 minutes.

questions.prompt: 2 pumpkins weigh the same as 6 apples. 1 apple weighs the same as 2 plums. How many plums weigh the same as 3 pumpkins?
questions.hint: How many apples does 1 pumpkin weigh?
questions.solution: 1 pumpkin = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 apples = 3 × 2 = 6 plums. So 3 pumpkins = 3 × 6 = 18 plums.

questions.prompt: Jada's average score on her first 4 math tests was 88. What score does she need on the 5th test so that her average for all 5 tests is 90?
questions.hint: Find the total points for 4 tests, and the total needed for 5 tests.
questions.solution: First 4 tests: 4 × 88 = 352 points. For an average of 90 on 5 tests she needs 5 × 90 = 450 points. 450 − 352 = 98.

questions.prompt: Bus A leaves the station every 12 minutes. Bus B leaves every 18 minutes. Both buses leave at 8:00 AM. At what time will they next leave together?
questions.hint: Find the smallest number that is a multiple of both 12 and 18.
questions.solution: Bus A: 12, 24, 36, … minutes. Bus B: 18, 36, … minutes. The first time both lists match is 36 minutes after 8:00 AM, which is 8:36 AM.

questions.prompt: Five squares, each with sides of 3 cm, are put together to make a plus sign as shown. What is the perimeter of the plus sign?
questions.hint: Count how many square sides are on the outside edge.
questions.solution: Each of the 4 arms shows 3 outside sides: 4 × 3 = 12 sides. The middle square has no outside sides. 12 × 3 cm = 36 cm.

questions.prompt: How many 3-digit numbers have digits that add up to 4?
questions.hint: Sort them by the hundreds digit: it can be 1, 2, 3 or 4.
questions.solution: Hundreds digit 1: 103, 112, 121, 130 (4). Hundreds digit 2: 202, 211, 220 (3). Hundreds digit 3: 301, 310 (2). Hundreds digit 4: 400 (1). Total: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

questions.prompt:
What is the sum of all the whole numbers from 1 to 50?
1 + 2 + 3 + … + 49 + 50
questions.hint: Pair 1 with 50, 2 with 49, and so on. How many pairs are there?
questions.solution: Each pair adds to 51: 1 + 50, 2 + 49, …, 25 + 26. There are 25 pairs. 25 × 51 = 1,275.

questions.prompt: In 5 years, Tia will be twice as old as she was 4 years ago. How old is Tia now?
questions.hint: The time from 4 years ago to 5 years from now is 9 years.
questions.solution: From 4 years ago to 5 years from now is 9 years. Her age then doubles, so her age 4 years ago was 9. Tia is 9 + 4 = 13. Check: in 5 years she is 18 = 2 × 9. ✓

questions.prompt: An open box (no lid) is 5 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm tall. What is the total area of the outside of the box (the bottom and the 4 sides)?
questions.hint: Find the area of the bottom, the two long sides and the two short sides.
questions.solution: Bottom: 5 × 4 = 20. Long sides: 2 × (5 × 3) = 30. Short sides: 2 × (4 × 3) = 24. Total: 20 + 30 + 24 = 74 sq cm.

questions.prompt: What is the fewest number of kids that must be in a room to be sure that at least 3 of them have birthdays in the same month?
questions.hint: How many kids could there be with no 3 sharing a month?
questions.solution: It's possible to have 2 kids in every month, which is 2 × 12 = 24 kids, with no 3 in the same month. One more kid makes 3 in some month. So 25 kids.

questions.prompt: Kim builds staircases out of squares. Step 1 uses 1 square, step 2 uses 1 + 2 = 3 squares, and step 3 uses 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 squares. How many squares does step 12 use?
questions.hint: Add 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 12. Pairing helps.
questions.solution: Step 12 uses 1 + 2 + … + 12 squares. Pair them: 1 + 12, 2 + 11, …, 6 + 7 gives 6 pairs of 13. 6 × 13 = 78 squares.
